title: Plus-Minus Digit Total
statement:
You get a positive integer n. Read its decimal digits from the most significant (leftmost) one. Give the first digit a plus sign, the second a minus sign, the third a plus sign, and so on, alternating.

Return the total.

examples.why: +4 − 7 + 1 − 2 = −4. Starting the signs from the last digit would give +2 − 1 + 7 − 4 = 4, the wrong sign.
+9 − 0 + 8 = 17. A zero still takes its turn in the sign pattern.
One digit, with a plus sign.

hints: The sign of a digit depends on its position counted from the left. What is awkward about taking digits off with % 10?
% 10 gives digits from the right. You can still alternate signs from the right and fix the result at the end. When does it need fixing?
If n has an even number of digits, the rightmost digit has a minus sign in the true answer, so negate the right-to-left total.

explain.intuition:
The rule counts from the left, but arithmetic hands you digits from the right (n % 10). Two ways out. Convert to a string and walk it left to right, flipping the sign each step. Or peel digits from the right with alternating signs starting at plus, and count them.

The right-to-left total has exactly the opposite sign of the true one when the digit count is even, because then the last digit should have had a minus sign. So negate it in that case.
steps: While n > 0: add sign · (n % 10), flip sign, increment count, and set n = ⌊n / 10⌋.
If count is even, return −sum; otherwise return sum.
pitfalls: Starting the signs from the rightmost digit without the parity fix. It gives the wrong sign for every number with an even digit count, like 4712.
Skipping zeros when alternating. Each digit, including 0, flips the sign for the next one.
Using n / 10 without Math.floor in JavaScript, which never reaches 0 cleanly.

complexity.space: O(1) arithmetic, O(digits) with a string

solutions.title: Walk the decimal string
solutions.idea: Convert n to a string and add digits left to right, flipping the sign each time.

solutions.title: Peel digits from the right, fix the sign
solutions.idea: Alternate signs from the rightmost digit, count the digits, and negate the total when the count is even.

followups: A number is divisible by 11 exactly when this alternating total is. Why?
n arrives as a string of 10^5 digits. Which solution still works?
